source_title: 6 PS2-Era Classics That Deserve A Comeback, Ranked
source_excerpt:
The PlayStation 2 remains a console that boasts years' worth of incredible gaming memories. It even served as many people's first introduction to video games. My first-ever console was the PlayStation 2 , and I'm still grateful for it to this day. Sony kept the system in production for a whopping 13 years, which helped the PS2 secure its spot as the best-selling console of all time.
With the ability to play games and also DVDs, the PS2 was a double dose of entertainment at the time. As great as the DVD functionality was, the true star was the games roster. Longtime fans all have their own ideas of what the best PS2 games are, but a few key titles went on to define the sixth console generation, even if you never got around to playing them. Despite their "iconic" status, some of these games are lying dormant and deserve a serious comeback.
Even though this list goes over games that helped define the PS2 era, they are not necessarily exclusive to the PS2 console.
Dungeon Crawling And City-Building Worthy Of A Second Chance
Honestly, when I was a kid, I thought Dark Cloud felt like a Legend of Zelda rip-off because of the box art character's uncanny resemblance to Link. However, that opinion changed when I finally played the game at a friend's house a few years later. Dark Cloud 's gameplay stands completely on its own. By today's standards, the controls are really clunky and outdated, but that's not exactly surprising for a game that's 25 years old.
It's best to look past how it has aged and focus on the mechanics that are perfect for a modern reboot. Dark Cloud 's dungeons are procedurally generated, and with games like No Man's Sky demonstrating how much farther this method has come, it would be pretty exciting to see what a reboot's dungeons could look like running on today's technology. Another core gameplay feature in Dark Cloud is rebuilding the game's world. Going back and forth between dungeon crawling and city-building creates a fun blend of challenge and creativity that would make a reboot extra compelling.
Before Horizon Zero Dawn and Horizon Forbidden West , Guerrilla Games had Killzone . Like many games from the PS2 era, Killzone may not have aged very well from a gameplay standpoint, but what it does still deliver on is its gritty, bleak atmosphere. Killzone 's world-building and lore remain deeply compelling, and it would be a great option for Sony to bring back from the grave.
If recent rumors turn out to be true, a new Killzone game could be on the way. Of course, claims this bold should be taken with a huge grain of salt, but these reports have sparked a little bit of hope in gamers with fond memories of playing the Killzone series. Only time will tell if this rumored new game is a Killzone remaster or a full-blown series reboot.
A Beautifully Unique Gothic Horror Western
Lazarus Malkoth boss fight on top of a train in Darkwatch
This is still one of the most underappreciated FPS games out there. Darkwatch has so many things going for it that would make for a great reboot: a western setting, gothic horror vibes, vampire curses, strong combat, and even a morality system. Also, the protagonist's name is Jericho Cross. It's pretty hard to get cooler than that.
Once a run-of-the-mill train robber trying to survive the unforgiving American frontier, Jericho is bitten by an ancient vampire lord and given vampiric abilities. There aren't enough horror games set in the Wild West , leaving plenty of room for Darkwatch to come back into the spotlight without risking oversaturation. If Darkwatch received a modern reboot, it would be like a blend of Bloodborne , Red Dead Redemption , and The Blood of Dawnwalker . That's a killer combo, but there doesn't seem to be any plans to bring this one-of-a-kind gothic horror FPS out of the vault.
A Heist Platformer Dripping With Charm
If I came across a genie that offered me three gaming-related wishes, one of them would be to bring Sly Cooper back, because I have some fantastic memories of playing this series. From the cel-shaded art style to the crew dynamics to the jazzy, noir-inspired atmosphere, there really isn't any other game quite like it. Thieves in Time was the most recent game in the franchise, and it ended everything on a baffling cliffhanger. That was 13 years ago, and there is currently no sign that points to Sony making space for a resolution.
Even with heavy hitters like Ghost of Tsushima and Infamous , the Sly Cooper series still makes for some of the best Sucker Punch games of all time. Nothing is impossible, but there doesn't seem to be much interest in bringing back Sly Cooper for now. With the way that stealth gameplay has evolved since the franchise's early days, there is untapped potential to create a new Sly Cooper game with a lot more gameplay depth.
Jak and Daxter doing a victory dance in Jak & Daxter: The Precursor Legacy
Jak and Dexter riding a ship across water in Jak & Daxter: The Precursor Legacy
Naughty Dog's Jak and Daxter is the first game I ever fell in love with. The platforming mechanics, level design, characters, and world-building all still hold up incredibly well for a game that came out in 2001. I still play it on my old PS2 to this day, and it always leaves me wondering what a modern version of the series would look like. The Jak and Daxter games grew more serious with each sequel, so it would be interesting to see how Naughty Dog would approach a reboot or a fourth mainline game.
The very first entry is still one of the best Naughty Dog games around, but the developer has shifted its tone significantly since 2001. Games like The Last of Us and Uncharted now define the studio, and new projects like the upcoming Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet continue to lean into that more mature vibe. If Naughty Dog ever returned to Jak and Daxter , it would be fascinating to see the team dive deeper into a gritty, dystopian story like Jak 2 and Jak 3, or pull back for something more lighthearted like The Precursor Legacy .
Rockstar is best known for Grand Theft Auto and Red Dead Redemption , but Bully is one of the developer's most iconic one-off games. Like a lot of games developed by Rockstar, Bully was marred by overreaction and controversy leading up to its release, which overshadowed a much deeper premise than many people were quick to assume. It has now been 20 years since its launch, and Bully 2 rumors have continued to crop up now and then.
After GTA 6 comes out, there's no telling what Rockstar has planned as its next project. A Bully sequel was reportedly in the works but never came to fruition. Rockstar giving a new Bully game a try isn't out of the question, but fans should keep their expectations low until the developer officially reveals its next project.
